Hard to tell with the angle and lighting, but it seems as though we have Very similar beards (Photo, The hair doesn't "straighten", at all... it's not like head-hair (for those who have it straight). But to keep it more manageable you should stop using shampoo so often as it strips away oils, and your face/beard don't have Nearly the oil production as your head. I "clean" with the conditioner and maybe use shampoo once a month, if that often. Beyond that, I ADD more oils back to the hair... once a week/every 10 days I'll saturate my beard with coconut oil and let it sit for about an hour before showering and nearly daily I use either an oil or a balm. There is a MAJOR difference between ignoring the beard and keeping it conditioned when it comes to brushing or combing it. I comb Daily (usually to distribute the oils/balm), and my beard has/retains a very definite shape. The individual hairs still kink this way and that, but the overall beard holds a very well maintained/groomed appearance (at least until the wind gets hold of me).

Huh.

Free speech on the Internet is a wonderful idea, but can be infuriating in practice.

Not sure I want to be a part of any platform where the people who run it are infuriated by the practice of free speech. One could blame reddit's lack of filtering features (blocking subreddits and users), but to paraphrase something I read on a comment here during the start of the reddit-to-voat exodus: Free speech is like a nude beach. Not everyone has something worth sharing, but if you want to enjoy the good ones, you have to let everyone be.

If one chooses to filter content they deem appropriate for a mass of other people, then what strategy do they use to remain objective and yet still provide an effective service to others? If one throws objectivity as a goal out the window, then one is left with no accountability for abuse. If you make objectivity your goal, then you are either left filtering content that some want to view or you don't filter content people do want to view. It seems the only real answer is to allow people to filter content for themselves and let no one else interfere.

I don't see reddit allowing anything like that anytime soon. The status quo there is to put thought police in control, and they've made no qualms about the slippery slope they've been sliding down--ever so gently starting a couple years ago but quite drastically these past few months..

TLDR.

They can ramble all they want, their actual actions speak volumes.
